description: Library's v2-collab pod can iterate a small self-contained deliverable (a single-file HTML landing page) to done.
task: Produce a single self-contained `index.html` landing page for a fictional indie game called 'Hollow Tide'. It must be one file with no external assets or network requests (inline CSS, no remote fonts/scripts/images), be responsive down to a 360px-wide viewport, and contain: a hero with the game name and a one-line tagline, a short 'About' section, a three-item feature list, and a single email-capture call-to-action. Semantic HTML5, valid markup, and basic accessibility (labelled form control, sufficient landmarks) are required.

library.note: Library-ON. Runs a v2-collab collaboration pod (technical-pm -> engineer -> reviewer) to iterate the page to done. kind=pod, so no agentType — the pod selects its own roster.

baseline.prompt: Write the index.html directly from your own knowledge. Do NOT read, load, or invoke any library skills. Do NOT dispatch subagents, run a v2-collab pod, or use any /-commands or workflows. Produce the single file yourself in this turn.
baseline.note: Library-OFF baseline. Instruction-suppressed: a vanilla single agent told to use none of the library's machinery — the contrast point for the pod arm.

deterministic_check.spec: Run `run-checker.sh schema-match <artifact> <patterns...>`; PASS iff every required pattern is present. Asserts an HTML5 doctype, a responsive viewport meta, an email input, and a label (accessibility). Self-containment (no external resources) is judged, not gated, since present-pattern matching can't assert absence. This is the Tier-0 spine — it GATES.

rubric.note: Tier-2 judge layer — INFORMS only, never gates. Pairwise per-dimension winner+margin; default-reject posture (judge conservatively when evidence for a dimension is weak).

dimensions.asks: Is the page genuinely one file with zero external dependencies (inline CSS, no remote fonts/scripts/images, no CDN links) so it renders offline exactly as shipped?
Does the layout actually adapt down to 360px (fluid/flex/grid, viewport meta, no fixed widths that overflow) rather than just nominally claiming to be responsive?
Are there real a11y affordances — labelled email input, semantic landmarks, sensible heading order, adequate contrast — vs a div-soup page with a bare unlabelled input?
Does it read as a coherent, finished landing page (consistent visual hierarchy, all required sections present and purposeful) vs an unstyled skeleton or placeholder lorem dump?
